text: I have funds in my joint Lake Michigan Credit Union ( LMCU ) checking account with my wife. She had an unpaid LMCU credit card that was a very small fraction of the total funds in the account. LMCU would not allow me to withdraw a small amount of funds because of the fractional charge on an account I am not on. LMCU denied disbursement because of a fractional charge that my wife had been trying to pay for the last month online. She didn't get to LMCU before they shut down all funds. We were unable to make it to LMCU during hours during a difficult period as my father passed away XX/XX/XXXX and had been actively transitioning since XX/XX/XXXX according to the hospice nurse. We tried to pay using the online tools but LMCU had technical issues sending the money from our joint checking account to her separate XXXX account. Note the amount that LMCU cancelled us over was < 1 % of the total funds they froze due to my wife 's unsuccessful attempts at paying. LMCU then removed all rewards she had on the credit card which totaled {$200.00}, well over the amount LMCU froze all funds for. Since they took these terrible consumer threatening actions we closed our credit accounts and are actively working to move our funds out of this place because of their terrible company policy that keeps funds away from the consumer for very fractional amount of funds. As a consumer I am appalled that my funds ( ie paycheck used to operate my family expenses ) was froze and restricted from me for a fractional amount that was late and that I was not associated with. This practice was highly impactful for our family and law should be made if not already to ensure these institutions don't continue to threaten hard working American consumers.
